title: Enable Shadow Traffic for internal dogfood tenants + create initial experiments + track findings
creator: Ethan Park
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Goal
Enable Shadow Traffic (mirrored requests + async scoring) for internal Redwood tenants so we can validate end-to-end behavior under real traffic before opening beta to Dedicated customers. This includes: feature flag enablement, default-safe policy configuration, creating initial shadow experiments on a small set of internal routes, and capturing issues + follow-ups.

Scope
1) Tenant enablement
- Enable feature flags for internal tenants ("redwood-internal" + "console-dogfood")
- Verify RBAC: only admins can create/modify shadow experiments + shadow policies
- Ensure audit logging is on for experiment create/update/delete

2) Create initial shadow experiments (dogfood)
- Pick 2–3 representative routes:
  a) Chat/completions (non-streaming) with typical SaaS workload
  b) Embeddings or rerank (if supported by shadowing v1) OR a second chat route with longer context
  c) One streaming route (if ENG-5414 is ready; otherwise defer)
- For each route: run control vs candidate variant shadowing with 0.5–1.0% sampling, fail-open required.
- Pin rubric version and record it in the experiment notes so we don’t compare across rubric changes.

3) Observability + guardrails validation
- Validate no impact to user-path p99 latency beyond guardrail budget.
- Validate circuit breaker behavior when scoring queue lags (shadow drops should not page user-path).
- Validate telemetry cardinality limits with real labels/route IDs.

4) Track issues + feed back into backlog
- Collect dogfood findings in this ticket and spin follow-ups with owners (routing, telemetry, scoring, console UX, docs).

Non-goals
- External customer enablement.
- Custom customer-provided eval code execution.

Acceptance criteria
- Internal tenants have shadow traffic flags enabled and documented.
- At least two shadow experiments created and running for >= 24 hours, with visible deltas in Console.
- Confirmed fail-open behavior with an induced failure (shadow target timeout and scoring backlog).
- No sustained cardinality alerts in metrics stack; any transient spikes are understood and mitigated.
- Issues found are filed as Linear follow-ups with clear repro steps and owners.
implementation_notes:
Enablement steps (internal)
- Feature flags:
  - shadow_traffic_enabled = true
  - console_shadow_experiments_ui = true
  - shadow_scoring_async_pipeline = true
  - audit_log_shadow_experiments = true
- Default-safe policy knobs for dogfood:
  - sampling_rate: 0.5% (start), max 1.0% without SRE sign-off
  - shadow_request_timeout_ms: 1500 (hard), no retries on dataplane
  - shadow_fail_open: true
  - shadow_headers_behavior: strip internal-only headers; allowlist trace headers
  - retention: short (default) + redaction enabled

Suggested dogfood experiment setups
- Experiment A (non-streaming): Control=model A (current pinned), Shadow=candidate model/quant profile; metrics: format adherence + refusal rate + rubric overall.
- Experiment B (second route): Shadow=alternate routing policy (e.g., different region or fallback ordering) to validate routing variant IDs + telemetry joins.

What to watch
- scoring_queue_lag_seconds
- shadow_mirror_drop_rate (circuit breaker)
- shadow_target_timeout_rate
- ingestion_write_failures
- prompt_redaction_error_rate / redaction_applied_rate
- console aggregates freshness (last_scored_at)
dogfood_plan:
Timeline
- Day 0: Enable flags + create experiments with 0.5% sampling.
- Day 1: Validate basic data flow (events -> storage -> scoring -> aggregates -> Console charts).
- Day 2: Increase one experiment to 1.0% sampling if SLOs are green.
- Day 3: Run failure drills (shadow target timeout + scoring backlog) and validate fail-open + alerting.

Routes/tenants (internal)
- Tenant: redwood-internal (primary)
- Tenant: console-dogfood (secondary)
- Routes: internal-chat-default, internal-support-assistant (if available)

Owners
- Enablement/flags: Benji Okafor
- Console experiments UX correctness: Chloe Martin
- Telemetry validation: Nadia Rahman
- SRE validation + failure drills: Sean Gallagher
- Scoring calibration sanity: Jonas Weber
findings_summary:
Findings from dogfood (Jan–Feb 2026)
1) Scoring queue lag incident during peak internal traffic
- Symptoms: aggregates stale for ~45 min; Console showed “data delayed” banner but drilldown examples intermittently empty.
- Mitigation: enabled backpressure/circuit breaker thresholds earlier; raised worker concurrency for internal tenant.
- Follow-up: ENG-xxxx to improve Console messaging + retries for example fetch; SRE to tune alert thresholds.

2) Cardinality spike from route_version tag
- Root cause: route_version emitted as full git SHA in one service; exceeded intended dimension policy.
- Fix: bucketed route_version to short semantic version; added validation to drop unknown tag values.
- Follow-up: ENG-5410 already tracking guardrails; ensure regression test in metrics dimension suite.

3) Partial shadow capture for streaming requests was confusing
- Console examples showed truncated outputs without clear “partial capture” indicator.
- Follow-up: add explicit fields/labels in example viewer and metric computation to exclude partials by default.

4) RBAC edge case
- Non-admin internal user could view examples (redacted) but shouldn’t have access under proposed enterprise posture.
- Fix: tightened permission check to require “Quality Experiments: Viewer” role.
- Follow-up: confirm alignment with Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin on default roles for beta.
